SCRIPT: Intraday, swing, or F and O? Here is what each one really means, with real trades from last week.
Intraday means you buy and sell on the same day. On the eleventh of November, Kalyan Jewellers opened at six hundred and thirty rupees, and hit six hundred and eighty nine within an hour.
But an intraday trade must close the same day. By the closing bell, it had slipped back to six hundred and sixty four.
Swing trading means holding for a few days or weeks. From the Diwali close of five hundred and ninety two, Kalyan reached seven hundred and eleven in three sessions. That is twenty percent.
The risk? You hold overnight. The very next morning it opened at seven hundred and eighteen, and dropped to six hundred and eighty five in fifteen minutes.
F and O means futures and options: contracts on a stock or an index, traded in fixed lots. One Nifty lot is sixty five units, about sixteen and a half lakh rupees of Nifty.
This morning, Nifty futures rose one hundred and seventy nine points. That is about eleven thousand six hundred rupees on one lot, and the same loss if you bet the other way.
That leverage is why SEBI found nearly nine in ten F and O traders lost money.
So which one do you do? Comment intraday, swing, or F and O, and save this for later.
